topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: When the will was read, the room went colder than a January sunrise. Siblings, they say blood's the thickest, but you see a lot of that blood turn to water when there's a house on the line. Especially this house—downtown, just a stone’s throw from the river. The paint’s peeling, sure, but it’s got bones like a prizefighter. I watched as they sized each other up, polite as poison, each waiting for the other to blink. In my line of work, you learn to read the small stuff. The way one hand twitches a little too close to the pocket, the flicker in the eye that says they’re already counting their share. I got a bad feeling about this one, but then, I get that a lot these days.
